decisions.evidenceText: the fall does not explain the proclivity to sin because Eve already had it.
decisions.rationale: The positive attribution-error rule applies because the move explicitly says the fall is wrongly credited with explaining something Eve already possessed. The default would require no defect without an explicit cue, but “does not explain” supplies that cue; invalid-inference is excluded because the stated defect is mistaken explanatory attribution, not merely a conclusion that fails to follow.

decisions.evidenceText: they'll be in the comment section right now saying, "Well, I went from Christianity to Islam."
decisions.rationale: The positive exact-proposition rule applies because the reverse-conversion example directly contests whether the cited changed lives count against treating religious satisfaction as interchangeable. The default is none when contact rests only on topic overlap or implication; none is excluded here because the response expressly supplies the opposing directional case.

decisions.evidenceText: Yeah, there's people that would have gone the other way
decisions.rationale: The positive component-contact-precludes-contrary rule governs because the response explicitly contacts the second component by presenting reverse conversions as the countercase to its evidentiary claim. The default relevant-no-component applies only when no component receives positive contact, so that classification is excluded once the exact-proposition contact is established.
